faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What is a token and where is it used?
faq.a1: Tokens are digital currency used to submit song requests on the PlayMyJam platform. They are valid only for song requests at venues using PlayMyJam; they cannot be converted to cash or transferred outside the platform. The balance is shared across all PlayMyJam venues.
faq.q2: How is the payment made, and is it secure?
faq.a2: Payments are processed via credit card or debit card through a 256-bit SSL encrypted connection. Your card details are not stored with us; transactions run through licensed payment institution infrastructure.
faq.q3: When will my tokens be credited to my account?
faq.a3: Instant. Tokens are a digital product — they are loaded into your balance the second your payment is confirmed, and you can start requesting songs right away. No shipping or waiting times.
faq.q4: Do I have a right to a refund?
faq.a4: Yes. If you haven't used any of the tokens in the package, you can request a refund within 14 days of the purchase date. Also, if your song request is rejected by the venue, any spent tokens will be automatically refunded to your balance. Details can be found on the Delivery and Return Terms page.
faq.q5: How much will my song request cost in tokens?
faq.a5: The number of tokens required for normal and priority queue requests is determined by the venue and is clearly displayed on the screen before submitting a request. Priority requests are moved to the front of the queue.
faq.q6: How can I use PlayMyJam for my venue?
faq.a6: Simply contact us via the email or phone in the contact section. No extra hardware is required for setup; the venue's existing screen/speaker setup and a browser are enough.

blocked.title: Notifications are blocked on this device
blocked.intro: Browser rules stop us from asking again here; you need to allow it once in your device settings. Come back to this screen afterwards — we'll take care of the rest.
blocked.androidApp: Phone Settings → Apps → find this app (it appears under the venue's name) → Notifications → allow.
blocked.androidBrowser: In Chrome, tap the lock icon in the address bar → Permissions (or Site settings) → Notifications → Reset.
blocked.ios: Phone Settings → Notifications → pick this app from the list → Allow Notifications.
blocked.desktop: Click the lock icon in the address bar → Notifications → Allow, then reload the page.
blocked.stillBlocked: Permission still looks off. Make sure the setting is saved and try again.
blocked.recovered: Notifications are on — you're all set.
